name: Reliquary-March

civilization.name: Sareth Dominion
civilization.notes: An atomic-era theocracy that sealed its most sacred artifacts in desert vaults shortly before annihilating itself in a three-day nuclear exchange.

specific_features: Ancient alien ruins: the reliquary vaults—forty seal-buried complexes arranged in a grid so vast it is only visible from orbit
Radiation hotspots: war-scarred craters that still glow on geiger counters centuries after the Dominion's final exchange
description: Rust-orange dunes march without end beneath a sky the color of old brass, broken only by the fossil channels of rivers that died before human ships ever flew. By day the horizon shimmers and lies; by night the temperature collapses and the sand contracts with sharp, gunshot cracks. A single ancient meteor crater anchors the western dust sea like a second, older sun printed into the ground.

Wind is the only voice here, and it speaks constantly—a dry hiss that finds every seam in a suit and never quite stops. Noon is white glare and heat that presses down like a hand; dusk brings a violet chill that makes the dead riverbeds look freshly cut. Everything smells faintly of ozone and scorched iron, though whether that is the planet or its history is hard to say.

Forty vaults lie buried across the march in a geometric grid, each sealed by the Sareth Dominion in the final weeks before its three-day self-destruction, each built to hold something the theocracy considered holier than survival. The war's craters still tick with residual radiation, yet the vaults themselves read perfectly clean—as if deliberately shielded, or deliberately spared. No excavated reliquary has ever been opened on-world; all forty were sealed from the inside.

The uranium wealth of the March funds three rival excavation charters, and all three have lost drones descending past the vaults' inner seals, each logging instrument failures at identical depths. The prevailing theory holds the Sareth entombed weapons; the dissenting theory, held quietly by those who have stood inside an unopened antechamber, is that they entombed guardians. Last season, one previously dormant hotspot began cooling in perfect sync with another four hundred kilometers away, and the diggers have started asking what, exactly, is drawing the power.
